name: Museum of Islamic Art
records_note: The Museum of Islamic Art has no records of its own; parent Qatar Museums posts no reports, accounts or sponsors but lists eight trustees.

name: Museum of West African Art (MOWAA)
funding: Founding partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.
watch: Oba loyalists disrupted the 9 November 2025 preview. Edo's Assembly urged a state takeover on 22 December 2025.
why_flagged: Founding partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.
records_note: It names donors by tier (undated) and eight trustees, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Musée d'Orsay
watch: A September 2025 analysis says taxpayers bore about 90% of LVMH's gift. Epstein's 2012 visit and Leon Black's 2014 loan are not flagged.
why_flagged: A September 2025 analysis says taxpayers bore about 90% of LVMH's gift. Epstein's 2012 visit and Leon Black's 2014 loan are not flagged.
records_note: Activity reports 2006 to 2025 with an aggregated income statement are on the EPMO site, patrons are undated logo clouds, and the board is listed.

name: Mystetskyi Arsenal
funding: State enterprise. 2025: UAH 38.0M state budget, UAH 24.2M own income. Project partners include Erste Foundation, British Council, the US Embassy and International Renaissance Foundation.
watch: In July 2013 the director had Volodymyr Kuznetsov's painting painted black and Vasyl Tsagolov's work excluded; artists called a boycott. 2025 visitors: 53,870.
why_flagged: State enterprise. 2025: UAH 38.0M state budget, UAH 24.2M own income. Project partners include Erste Foundation, British Council, the US Embassy and International Renaissance Foundation.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2017 to 2025 and audited statements for 2014 to 2019; the 2025 report names partners; no board is listed.

name: Nafasi Art Space
funding: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), Royal Norwegian Embassy, self-generated arts income; non-profit trust.
watch: TotalEnergies Tanzania partners on its VIA Creative programme.
why_flagged: TotalEnergies Tanzania partners on its VIA Creative programme.
records_note: It names its donors and supporters with funding years but posts no annual reports or accounts, and describes its board without naming anyone.

name: Nairobi National Museum
funding: National Museums of Kenya, a state corporation, runs it. Planet Africa (2024 to 2025) was funded by the German Research Foundation and Germany's Foreign Office.
watch: In May 2017 museum management pulled works by Michael Soi, Patrick Mukabi and Bertiers Mbatia on opening day, saying they were unsuitable for children.
why_flagged: Run by National Museums of Kenya, a state corporation. The Planet Africa project (opened November 2024) lists the German Research Foundation and Germany's Foreign Office as funders. No sponsor list.
records_note: No records of its own: parent National Museums of Kenya posts annual reports for 2015 to 2019 and names its board; no accounts or donors.

name: Nam June Paik Art Center
funding: Gyeonggi Province, through the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation. Hyundai Motor sponsors its Trans-Local exhibition series (KRW 600M over three years, announced 2025). Free admission.
watch: Hyundai subsidiary SMART Alabama hired children as young as 12 (Reuters, 2022). Same Hyundai ruling as MMCA applies.
why_flagged: Gyeonggi Province, through the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation. Hyundai Motor sponsors its Trans-Local exhibition series (KRW 600M over three years, announced 2025). Free admission.
records_note: Its parent foundation posts yearbooks for 2012 to 2025, settlement papers and a named board; the centre shows sponsor logos only, undated.

name: Nasjonalmuseet (National Museum of Norway)
funding: State-funded foundation; 2024 income NOK 1,059M, gifts NOK 12.5M. Fredriksen Family Art Company lends its collection on a ten-year deal and funds four PhDs. AKO Foundation and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB give.
watch: June 2022 appeal urged ending the Fredriksen deal; critics cite Seadrill's 2014 Rosneft contract. The museum sees no reason for review.
why_flagged: State-funded foundation; 2024 income NOK 1,059M, gifts NOK 12.5M. Fredriksen Family Art Company lends its collection on a ten-year deal and funds four PhDs. AKO Foundation and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB give.
records_note: Annual reports run from 2003 to 2025, accounts are filed in the Norwegian register, partners are named without a date, and the board is listed.

name: National Art Gallery of Namibia
funding: State-owned art gallery. Bank Windhoek partners on its 2025/2026 Triennial.
watch: In March 2014 the gallery asked artist Paolo Solari Bozzi to withdraw photos of Himba girls; he pulled the whole show. The gallery denied censorship.
why_flagged: In March 2014 the gallery asked artist Paolo Solari Bozzi to withdraw photos of Himba girls; he pulled the whole show. The gallery denied censorship.
records_note: NAGN posts annual reports for 2019/20 to 2024/25 with audited statements, names its seven trustees, and names its strategic partners in the latest report.

name: National Art Museum of the Republic of Belarus
funding: Direct state budget of the Republic of Belarus under the presidential administration.
watch: State museum founded 1939, with 30,000+ objects, at Lenina 20. Its 'Exhibition of One Masterpiece: Marc Chagall, A Stroll' (8 Apr–21 Sep 2026), lent by the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg, is sponsored by Sber Bank (Belarus). It ran a Belgazprombank 'Autumn Salon' partnership in the 2010s.

records_note: The museum's site lists administration and documents but no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or governing board.

name: National Art Museum of Ukraine
funding: State museum. The Cabinet gave it UAH 5.6M in 2020 for emergency facade repairs. Donations go to its own charitable foundation.
watch: In October 2012 staff sent an open letter demanding the removal of acting director Tatiana Mironova; art workers backed it with a statement and petition.
why_flagged: State museum. The Cabinet gave it UAH 5.6M in 2020 for emergency facade repairs. Donations go to its own charitable foundation. No corporate sponsor list is published.
records_note: Its public information page holds a 2021 budget and utility compliance notes only; no annual report, accounts, donor list or board.

name: National Galleries of Scotland
funding: £24M. Scottish Government grant-in-aid, Baillie Gifford, trusts and individual patrons.
watch: Kept Baillie Gifford under protest; dropped BP 2019.
why_flagged: Kept Baillie Gifford under protest; dropped BP 2019.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2023-24, names corporate supporters and donors on site pages, and OSCR lists its 12 trustees.
